newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank hikes repo rate by 20 bps to 9.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank hikes repo rate by 20 bps to 9.0 pct.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Wednesday said it had raised its bill repurchase rate by 20 basis points to 9.0 percent, but left the reverse repo rate unchanged at 7.2 percent.
Peter Andresic, chief dealer at the NBS, told Reuters the move was prompted by an increase in the accepted yield in the finance ministry's treasury bill auction.
"But we also express dissatisfaction with current developments in banks' bids interest rate level which, if continued, could force us to use further administrative instruments," Andresic said.
Average yield at the Slovak Finance Ministry's four-week treasury bill auction earlier on Wednesday hit 8.98 percent, up from 8.77 percent in the last auction of similar bills.

The repo hike followed two central bank liquidity bill auctions. One auction of two-month bills with yield set at 10.59 percent was successful. The other, involving three-month bills, failed as the central bank refused all bids.
The NBS has raised the repo rate three times in the past two weeks by a total of 80 basis points.
